article.title: Why AI Systems Need Versioned Prompts and Tools
article.why: 把 prompt、tool schema、evaluation 與 rollback 視為 production release，適合 AI 工程與治理學習。
article.author: OpenAI learning editor

paragraphs.en:
AI systems are often changed without anyone thinking of the change as a new software release. A team may edit a system prompt, rename a tool, add an API parameter, change a retrieval setting, or replace one model with another. Each change can alter behavior. If the system does not record which versions were active, debugging becomes much harder.

Imagine an AI agent that worked well on Monday but began making incorrect updates on Wednesday. The model name is the same, so the team first assumes nothing important changed. Later, they discover that a tool description was rewritten on Tuesday. The new wording caused the agent to select an update tool in cases where it previously used a read-only search tool. Without version history, the team may spend hours investigating the wrong component.

Versioning creates traceability. A production request should be associated with the model version, system prompt version, tool schema version, retrieval configuration, and any important policy configuration that influenced the result. This does not require storing every piece of infrastructure in one file. It requires a reliable way to reconstruct the configuration that produced an action.

Prompts deserve version control because small wording changes can have large effects. A prompt can be treated like code: changes are reviewed, labeled, tested, and linked to a release. Teams can compare a new prompt against a fixed evaluation set before deployment. If performance gets worse, they can roll back quickly instead of trying to remember the previous wording.

Tool definitions need the same discipline. An agent chooses tools partly from names, descriptions, parameters, and examples. Changing any of these can change selection behavior even when the underlying API is unchanged. A new required parameter can also create failures if the model was not tested against it. Tool schemas should therefore have explicit versions and compatibility rules.

Versioning also supports incident analysis. Logs become more useful when they show not just what the agent did, but what configuration was in force. Investigators can ask whether a failure began after a particular prompt release, model upgrade, retrieval change, or permission-policy update. This turns a vague behavioral problem into a testable engineering hypothesis.

Not every change needs a complex approval process. Low-risk experiments can move quickly. The principle is that production behavior should be reproducible enough to investigate. Teams should know what changed, when it changed, who approved it, and how to restore the previous state.

AI systems are probabilistic, so exact outputs may still vary. Versioning does not make them deterministic. It creates a stable record of the conditions around that variation. Better observability, controlled releases, and clear rollback paths make AI systems easier to operate as real production systems rather than collections of prompts that quietly evolve over time.

Evaluation results should be versioned too. If a team reports that an agent achieved 92 percent task success, the number should be tied to the evaluation dataset and scoring rules used at that time. Otherwise, a later team may compare 92 percent with 95 percent even though the test set changed. A release record can connect configuration, evaluation, and deployment in one chain.

This discipline is especially useful when several teams share the same agent platform. One team may update a common retrieval service while another changes a prompt. Without coordinated version identifiers, a performance shift can be wrongly attributed to the most visible change. Release metadata helps separate simultaneous changes.

A simple starting point is enough: assign identifiers to prompts and tool schemas, record them in logs, test changes before production, and keep the previous version available for rollback. The goal is not bureaucracy. It is to make change observable.
paragraphs.zh:
AI 系統經常被修改，卻沒有被當成一次正式 software release。團隊可能改 system prompt、重新命名 tool、增加 API parameter、調整 retrieval setting，或更換 model；任何一項都可能改變行為。如果系統沒有記錄當時使用的版本，之後 debug 就會非常困難。

例如某 Agent 週一運作正常、週三開始錯誤更新資料。Model 名稱沒有變，團隊一開始以為沒有重大變更；後來才發現週二有人改寫了 tool description，導致 Agent 在原本應使用 read-only search 的情況選到 update tool。沒有 version history 時，團隊可能花很多時間查錯元件。

Versioning 的價值在 traceability。每個 production request 應能對應 model version、system prompt version、tool schema version、retrieval configuration 與重要 policy configuration。目的不是把所有東西塞進一個檔案，而是能可靠重建「當時是哪一組設定產生這個行動」。

Prompt 也應像 code 一樣有 version control：修改要 review、標記、測試並連結 release。新 prompt 上 production 前可以用固定 evaluation set 比較；performance 變差時，能快速 rollback，而不是靠記憶猜之前的 wording。

Tool definition 也需要同樣紀律。Agent 會依 tool name、description、parameter、example 選工具，這些內容改變就可能改變 selection behavior，即使底層 API 沒變。新增 required parameter 也可能造成失敗，因此 tool schema 要有明確 version 與 compatibility rules。

Versioning 也支援 incident analysis。Log 不只要記錄 Agent 做了什麼，也要記錄當時 configuration。如此才能確認問題是否從某次 prompt release、model upgrade、retrieval change 或 permission-policy update 開始，把模糊的行為問題變成可測試的 engineering hypothesis。

不是每個變更都需要繁重 approval。低風險 experiment 可以快速，但 production behavior 必須有足夠 reproducibility 以便調查：知道改了什麼、何時改、誰批准、如何恢復前一版。

AI 本質是 probabilistic，versioning 不會讓輸出完全 deterministic；它只是為變異建立穩定背景紀錄。Evaluation result 也應版本化，例如 92% task success 必須綁定當時的 dataset 與 scoring rules，否則後來拿 95% 比較時，可能其實 test set 已經變了。

多團隊共享同一 Agent platform 時尤其需要這種 discipline，因為 retrieval service 與 prompt 可能同時被不同團隊修改。最簡單的起點就是：替 prompt/tool schema 編號、寫入 log、上線前測試，並保留可 rollback 的前一版。目的不是 bureaucracy，而是讓 change observable。
paragraphs.ja:
AI systemは変更されても、新しいsoftware releaseとして扱われないことがあります。system promptの編集、tool名変更、API parameter追加、retrieval setting変更、model交換はいずれも挙動を変える可能性があります。どのversionが有効だったか記録しなければdebugは難しくなります。

例えば月曜まで正常だったAgentが水曜から誤更新を始めたとします。model名は同じでも、火曜にtool descriptionが変更され、read-only searchではなくupdate toolを選ぶようになった可能性があります。version historyがなければ間違ったcomponentを長時間調査することになります。

Versioningはtraceabilityを作ります。production requestとmodel version、system prompt version、tool schema version、retrieval configuration、policy configurationを結びつけ、当時の設定を再構成できるようにします。

Promptもcodeのようにreview、label、test、releaseへ紐付けます。固定evaluation setで比較し、悪化したら前versionへrollbackできるようにします。Tool definitionも同じで、name、description、parameter、exampleの変更だけでもselection behaviorが変わるため、schema versionとcompatibility ruleが必要です。

Incident analysisでは、何をしたかだけでなく、どのconfigurationで実行したかをlogに残します。prompt release、model upgrade、retrieval change、permission-policy updateのどこからfailureが始まったか検証しやすくなります。

すべての変更を重いapproval processにする必要はありません。ただしproduction behaviorは調査できる程度に再現可能であるべきです。何を、いつ、誰が変え、どう戻すかを把握します。

AIはprobabilisticなのでversioningで完全にdeterministicにはなりませんが、変動の条件を安定して記録できます。Evaluation結果もdatasetとscoring ruleに紐付けてversioningしないと、92%と95%を比較してもtest setの違いかもしれません。複数teamでplatformを共有する場合は特に有効です。まずpromptとtool schemaへIDを付け、logに残し、production前にtestし、前versionをrollback可能にするだけでも十分な出発点になります。
